title: Fish Shish Kabob with Vegetables (No Potatoes)

content.title: About
content.content: Fish shish kabob with vegetables is a dish where chunks of fish (commonly salmon or cod) are threaded onto skewers together with a mix of vegetables (bell pepper, zucchini, onion, cherry tomatoes) and grilled or baked. Potatoes are omitted, making the meal lighter and lower in carbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fish kebabs are a staple in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines.
The vegetables used are rich in antioxidants that help protect cells from oxidative stress.
Grilling preserves most of the omega‑3 fatty acids in the fish.
The recipe can be adapted for dietary needs by swapping fish for seafood or tofu.
Excluding potatoes lowers the glycemic index of the dish, beneficial for blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Fish, especially salmon and mackerel, provides EPA and DHA – fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: A serving delivers about 20‑25 g of protein, essential for muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fish and vegetables supply B12, B6, and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish contains selenium, iodine, magnesium, and potassium, which aid thyroid function and nerve health.

items.title: Vegetable antioxidants
items.content: Bell peppers and tomatoes are high in vitamin C and lycopene, helping combat free radicals.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Certain fish can contain mercury or cadmium; choose reputable sources and limit intake to 2‑3 servings per week.

items.title: Over‑cooking
items.content: Excessive charring can create acrylamide in vegetables; aim for a golden brown, not blackened, finish.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the kabob hot, straight from the grill, with a squeeze of lemon, a yogurt‑herb sauce, or fresh parsley. It pairs well with a side salad, cauliflower rice, or whole‑grain couscous.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in the oven or on a skillet rather than the microwave to retain texture.
